Requester meaning: independently choose a random, complex photographic concept that tests the updated wardrobe-related themes, use the attached image, and evaluate an actual generation. Agent-owned realization: a clockwork-moth cabaret performer releases a snagged cape at the theatre wing while the entrance opens. The fictional preceding snag, lifted weight, remaining tension and released edge connect to the bright destination on stage. The face and practical care lead; clothing construction and materials make that same moment richer. Saved sensual=1 gives subtle poised appeal, fetish=0 adds no erotic object treatment, surreal=0 keeps ordinary theatre physics, and creativity=1 develops restrained variation within the random concept. These particular role, place, garment, gesture, colors and framing are authorial, not requester specifications.

A richly layered photographic scene captures a person whose face and hair are guided by the supplied portrait, in a visible costume action with a readable material consequence. A cabaret performer stands in the narrow wing of a small theatre, just as the crimson curtain opens onto an amber lane of stage light. The portrait's soft facial outline, brown eyes, dark chin-length bob and fine center-parted fringe guide her visible appearance. She has turned her face toward the troublesome cape edge, lips gently parted in concentrated patience; the warmth on her cheek keeps her poised presence intimate and immediate. Her fitted forest-green velvet bodice has a softly curved neckline and cream organza puff sleeves. The velvet's dense dark pile absorbs the light while the sleeves hold pale translucent folds. A copper satin waist ribbon is tied into a compact bow over a deep teal pleated skirt. A midnight-blue satin cape hangs from two bronze moth brooches at her upper chest, joined by a short curved bronze chain; each end attaches visibly to one brooch. Amber organza inserts interrupt the dark cape panels, and raised copper embroidery follows branching moth-wing veins across those inserts. A narrow black scalloped lace border is sewn along the cape's lower edge. One bronze drop earring hangs from each visible ear, catching small warm highlights near her bob. The cape border has snagged on the outer corner of the black music stand beside her. Her right hand lifts a loose fold above the snag to take the fabric's weight, while her left thumb and forefinger ease one caught lace loop upward from the stand's corner. Both forearms connect visibly back to her shoulders; her elbows stay in the clear space beside her torso. The remaining loop is taut at the metal corner, and a newly released length of lace curls softly below her left hand. Her balanced stance lets the skirt settle into long downward folds. The open curtain and stage-light lane sit behind the freed cloth, giving the little practical struggle an immediate destination. Make a vertical environmental portrait from head to below the knees, observed nearby at chest height from slightly in front of her. Keep her face, hands, chest clasp and music-stand corner readable together. Cooler backstage fill preserves the green bodice and blue cape beside the amber stage glow; fine cloth weave, seam joins, skin texture and scuffed floor boards remain naturally photographic. The face leads, the fabric tension answers it, and the bright opening beyond is the third beat.

authorial_core.baseline_prompt_en: A richly layered photographic scene captures a person whose face and hair are guided by the supplied portrait, in a visible costume action with a readable material consequence. A cabaret performer stands in the narrow wing of a small theatre, just as the crimson curtain opens onto an amber lane of stage light. The portrait's soft facial outline, brown eyes, dark chin-length bob and fine center-parted fringe guide her visible appearance. She has turned her face toward the troublesome cape edge, lips gently parted in concentrated patience; the warmth on her cheek keeps her poised presence intimate and immediate. Her fitted forest-green velvet bodice has a softly curved neckline and cream organza puff sleeves. The velvet's dense dark pile absorbs the light while the sleeves hold pale translucent folds. A copper satin waist ribbon is tied into a compact bow over a deep teal pleated skirt. A midnight-blue satin cape hangs from two bronze moth brooches at her upper chest, joined by a short curved bronze chain; each end attaches visibly to one brooch. Amber organza inserts interrupt the dark cape panels, and raised copper embroidery follows branching moth-wing veins across those inserts. A narrow black scalloped lace border is sewn along the cape's lower edge. One bronze drop earring hangs from each visible ear, catching small warm highlights near her bob. The cape border has snagged on the outer corner of the black music stand beside her. Her right hand lifts a loose fold above the snag to take the fabric's weight, while her left thumb and forefinger ease one caught lace loop upward from the stand's corner. Both forearms connect visibly back to her shoulders; her elbows stay in the clear space beside her torso. The remaining loop is taut at the metal corner, and a newly released length of lace curls softly below her left hand. Her balanced stance lets the skirt settle into long downward folds. The open curtain and stage-light lane sit behind the freed cloth, giving the little practical struggle an immediate destination. Make a vertical environmental portrait from head to below the knees, observed nearby at chest height from slightly in front of her. Keep her face, hands, chest clasp and music-stand corner readable together. Cooler backstage fill preserves the green bodice and blue cape beside the amber stage glow; fine cloth weave, seam joins, skin texture and scuffed floor boards remain naturally photographic. The face leads, the fabric tension answers it, and the bright opening beyond is the third beat.
